subject: Oceanography
title: Microplastics
description: A quick, practical guide to Microplastics.

hook.text: Microplastics smaller than 5 mm are now found everywhere—from Arctic ice to the Mariana Trench.

buildup.text: They come from broken-down bottles, synthetic clothing fibers, tire dust, and cosmetic microbeads.

discovery.text: A single load of laundry can release 700,000 microfibers into the water—most too small for filters to catch.

twist.text: Microplastics absorb toxins from seawater—concentrating pollutants and delivering them to animals that eat them.

climax.text: Microplastics have been found in human blood, lungs, and placentas—the health effects are still unknown.

punchline.text: Plastic is now inside every ocean—and inside us.

quiz.question: How do microplastics enter the ocean from clothing?
